title: CS/Sales intake: bundle curation and initial economic scoping
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Sales and Customer Success send a stream of high-touch enterprise feature asks that are often overlapping across accounts, vary widely in implementation effort, and arrive without economic context. This causes: scattered scoping work, duplicated engineering discovery, and slow prioritization. Goal: build a lightweight bundle-curation and initial economic scoping workflow that lets PMs and Solutions Engineers rapidly cluster related asks, score bundles by estimated value and effort, and produce a 1-page scoping envelope for quick go/no-go decisions. This ticket scopes the playbook, scoring rubric, tooling touchpoints, and a two-week pilot with three AE/CS pods.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable 5-factor scoring rubric documented and agreed by PM, Sales engineering (SE), and solutions leadership
A one-page scoping envelope template created (cost/effort/risks/assumptions) and stored in Drive
Pilot run completed with 3 pods and 12 requests consolidated into <=4 bundles
Pilot produces time-to-decision metric: median initial scoping time <= 3 business days
Stakeholders sign-off on next-phase rollout plan
success_metrics: % reduction in duplicate engineering discovery across pilot bundles: target >= 40%
Median time from request to initial scoping envelope: target <= 3 business days
Percent of pilot bundles with plausible cost estimate band: target >= 85%
Correlation of proposed bundle score to eventual commercial interest (closed-won signals) tracked over 90 days
stakeholders: Legal / Security advisor: Ravi Kumar (spot consult)
proposed_flow: 1) CS/AE files intake form variant (minimal required fields) into intake board. 2) Weekly compact triage by CS+SE that clusters related asks into candidate bundles using similarity tags and business signals. 3) PM runs quick rubric score (see rubric) and drafts 1-page scoping envelope (low/med/high effort and cost range). 4) SE validates feasibility and flags security/regulatory concerns. 5) Bundle outcome: Quick yes -> pilot scoping in Squad, Yes-with-conditions -> deeper discovery, No -> standard decline with rationale. 6) Capture metrics and feedback for iteration.
decisions: Use a lightweight intake form (max 6 fields) to maximize signal while minimizing CS friction
Adopt a 5-factor scoring rubric (Account Value, Cross-Customer Demand, Implementation Effort, Security/Compliance Risk, Strategic Fit)
Scoring weights will be: Account Value 30, Cross-Customer Demand 25, Effort 25, Risk 10, Strategic Fit 10 (initial, pilot-only)
Output will be a 1-page scoping envelope with a 3-band cost estimate (low/likely/high) and suggested next-step
Pilot scope limited to non-bug feature requests only (no infra/legal-only asks)
Pilot duration: 6 weeks with a 2-week initial trial with 3 pods
rubric_example: Example: Three requests (A: custom routing rules; B: per-tenant KV caching; C: traffic-shaping UI) were clustered into Bundle X
Account Value: weighted average -> 8/10 (high MRR accounts attached)
Cross-Customer Demand: 6/10 (observed may apply to 12% of active accounts)
Effort: 5/10 (engineer estimation: 3-4 sprints total; moderate infra changes)
Risk: 3/10 (minor regulatory flags on per-tenant data isolation for one account)
Strategic Fit: 7/10 (aligns to roadmap theme 'dedicated controls')
Bundle score -> 67/100 -> Recommendation: 'Yes-with-conditions' -> Scoped MVP limited to routing + KV guardrails; UI deprioritized
deliverables: Intake form template (Google Forms + short doc)
Rubric doc with scoring definitions and examples (Drive)
Pilot run retrospective and dataset of intake->bundle mappings
Implementation feedback loop: lightweight dashboard tracking bundle lifecycle
